hook.line: Good essays go past the symptom to the cause underneath. Spanish talks about causes with the same plant picture as English, so this one feels familiar.
hook.es: El conflicto tiene su raíz en el reparto de tierras.
hook.en: The conflict has its roots in the distribution of land.

examples.es: El conflicto tiene su raíz en el reparto de tierras.
examples.en: The conflict has its roots in the distribution of land.

examples.es: Hay que cortar el problema de raíz.
examples.en: We have to tackle the problem at the root.

examples.es: Muchos problemas del barrio tienen su raíz en la falta de agua.
examples.en: Many of the neighbourhood's problems have their root in the lack of water.

examples.es: La desconfianza tiene su raíz en una vieja historia.
examples.en: Distrust has its root in an old story.

examples.es: Quieren arrancar de raíz la tradición del barrio.
examples.en: They want to uproot the neighbourhood's tradition completely.

examples.es: Hay que cortar de raíz el rumor.
examples.en: We have to put a stop to the rumour at the root.

rule:
*Tener su raíz en* + cause: the deep cause is the thing after *en*. The effect comes first, the cause second: *el conflicto tiene su raíz en el reparto de tierras*. Spanish usually keeps *raíz* singular, even with a plural subject: *tienen su raíz en*.

*De raíz* goes after *cortar*, *arrancar* or *atacar* and means getting rid of something completely, at its source. No article: *de raíz*, not *de la raíz*.
smallPrint: Teachers call these figurative uses of *raíz*. The related *la semilla de* names the small beginning of something that grew.

readAndPick.es: El conflicto tiene su raíz en el reparto de tierras.
options: The conflict has its roots in the distribution of land.
The conflict will end the distribution of land.
The distribution of land has its roots in the conflict.

readAndPick.es: Hay que cortar el problema de raíz.
options: We have to ignore the problem.
We have to wait for the problem.
We have to tackle the problem at the root.

readAndPick.es: Muchos problemas tienen su raíz en la falta de agua.
options: Many problems are the root of the lack of water.
Many problems have their root in the lack of water.
Many problems cause water.

readAndPick.es: La falta de agua tiene su raíz en la mala gestión.
options: Poor management comes from the lack of water.
The lack of water comes from poor management.
Poor management cuts the water.

readAndPick.es: La desconfianza tiene su raíz en una vieja historia.
options: Distrust has its root in an old story.
An old story has its root in distrust.
Distrust ends an old story.

readAndPick.es: Quieren arrancar de raíz la tradición del barrio.
options: They want to plant the neighbourhood's tradition.
They want to uproot the neighbourhood's tradition completely.
They want to sell the neighbourhood's tradition.

readAndPick.es: Hay que cortar de raíz el rumor.
options: We have to put a stop to the rumour at the root.
We have to repeat the rumour.
We have to cut the rumour a little.

readAndPick.es: El miedo tiene su raíz en la desconfianza.
options: Distrust has its root in fear.
Fear has its root in distrust.
Fear is the root of distrust.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *en* or *de* and type the whole sentence: *El conflicto tiene su raíz ___ el reparto de tierras.*
yourTurn.answer: El conflicto tiene su raíz en el reparto de tierras.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Distrust has its roots in an old story.
yourTurn.answer: La desconfianza tiene su raíz en una vieja historia.
accept: La desconfianza tiene su raíz en una historia vieja.
yourTurn.why: Effect first, then *tiene su raíz en* + the cause.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: We have to tackle the problem at the root.
yourTurn.answer: Hay que cortar el problema de raíz.
accept: Hay que atacar el problema de raíz.
yourTurn.why: *De raíz* has no article, and goes after the verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Many of the neighbourhood's problems have their root in the lack of water.
yourTurn.answer: Muchos problemas del barrio tienen su raíz en la falta de agua.
yourTurn.why: A plural subject takes *tienen*, but *raíz* stays singular.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The rumour has its root in an old argument.
yourTurn.answer: El rumor tiene su raíz en una vieja discusión.
accept: El rumor tiene su raíz en una discusión vieja.
yourTurn.why: Same frame: the rumour is the effect, the argument is the cause.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: They want to uproot the neighbourhood's tradition completely.
yourTurn.answer: Quieren arrancar de raíz la tradición del barrio.
yourTurn.why: *Arrancar de raíz* means to remove something completely.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural: *El problema tiene su raíz en el miedo.* Say: The problems have their root in fear.
yourTurn.answer: Los problemas tienen su raíz en el miedo.
yourTurn.why: Two things change: *los problemas* and *tienen*; *su raíz* stays.

pitfalls.wrong: El conflicto tiene su raíz de la injusticia.
pitfalls.right: El conflicto tiene su raíz en la injusticia.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The cause comes after *en*, not *de*.

pitfalls.wrong: Hay que cortar el problema de la raíz.
pitfalls.right: Hay que cortar el problema de raíz.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The fixed phrase is *de raíz*, with no article.

pitfalls.wrong: Hay que cortar el problema en raíz.
pitfalls.right: Hay que cortar el problema de raíz.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "at the root", but Spanish uses *de*.

personal: Think of a problem you know well and say where it comes from, starting with *Tiene su raíz en*.
